docs.title: Teams CLI
docs.text: Teams CLI is a command-line and TUI tool for interacting with Microsoft Teams.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• List, create, archive, unarchive, and delete teams.
  • Create channels with members from data files.
  • List chats and fetch messages.
  • Send channel and chat messages using templates or raw content.

docs.title: Shell completions
docs.text: Teams CLI uses Cobra, so you can generate shell completions with the built-in command.

docs.title: Bash completion
docs.text:
1. Generate completion script
./teams-cli completion bash > teams-cli-completion.bash
  1. Install system-wide (recommended)
sudo cp teams-cli-completion.bash /etc/bash_completion.d/
  1. Or install user-only
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions
cp teams-cli-completion.bash ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/teams-cli
  1. Reload your shell
source ~/.bashrc

docs.title: Zsh completion
docs.text:
1. Generate completion script
./teams-cli completion zsh > _teams-cli
  1. Install in Zsh function path
sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions
sudo cp _teams-cli /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/
  1. Or install user-only
mkdir -p ~/.zsh/completions
cp _teams-cli ~/.zsh/completions/
echo 'fpath=(~/.zsh/completions $fpath)' >> ~/.zshrc
echo 'autoload -U compinit && compinit' >> ~/.zshrc
  1. Reload your shell
source ~/.zshrc

docs.title: Fish completion
docs.text:
1. Generate and install completion
./teams-cli completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/teams-cli.fish
  1. Reload Fish configuration
source ~/.config/fish/config.fish

docs.title: PowerShell completion
docs.text:
1. Generate completion script
./teams-cli completion powershell > teams-cli.ps1
  1. Create PowerShell profile directory
mkdir -p (Split-Path $PROFILE)
  1. Add to PowerShell profile
Add-Content $PROFILE ". /path/to/teams-cli.ps1"
  1. Reload PowerShell
& $PROFILE

docs.title: Create
docs.text: Create channels from file

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Create multiple Teams channels with members from a data file (YAML/JSON/TOML/CSV).

The data file should contain channel definitions with channel_ref, role, and user_refs.

docs.title: Data file format
docs.text:
YAML example:

general:
  owners:
    - user.one@example.com
  members:
    - user.two@example.com
announcements:
  owners:
    - user.three@example.com
  members: []

JSON example:

{
  "general": {
    "owners": ["user.one@example.com"],
    "members": ["user.two@example.com"]
  },
  "announcements": {
    "owners": ["user.three@example.com"],
    "members": []
  }
}

TOML example:

[general]
owners = ["user.one@example.com"]
members = ["user.two@example.com"]

[announcements]
owners = ["user.three@example.com"]
members = []

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: teams-cli channels create [flags]

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
--data string          Path to channels data file (YAML/JSON/TOML/CSV)
      --dry-run              Preview only
      --ensure-in-channels   Ensure members are in channels
      --ensure-in-team       Ensure members are in team
  -h, --help                 help for create
      --team string          Name of the team

docs.title: Create Single
docs.text: Create single team

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: This command creates a single team based on provided flags and a simplified data file.

docs.title: Data file format
docs.text:
CSV example:

role,user_ref
owner,user.one@example.com
owner,user.two@example.com

YAML example:

description: "Example team"
owners:
  - user.one@example.com
members:
  - user.two@example.com

JSON and TOML formats are also supported with the same fields as the YAML example.

You can also provide the description via the --description flag instead of the file.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: teams-cli teams create-single [flags]

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
--description string   Description of the team
      --dry-run              Preview only
  -f, --file string          Path to members data file
  -h, --help                 help for create-single
  -i, --include-me           Include current user
      --team-name string     Name of the team to create
      --visibility string    Visibility (private/public)

docs.title: Create
docs.text: Create teams from file

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Create multiple Teams from a data file (YAML/JSON/CSV).

The data file should contain team definitions with display names, descriptions, owners, and members.

docs.title: Data file format
docs.text:
YAML example:

engineering:
  description: "Engineering team"
  owners:
    - user.one@example.com
  members:
    - user.two@example.com
ops:
  description: "Operations team"
  visibility: "public"
  owners:
    - user.three@example.com
  members: []

JSON example:

{
  "engineering": {
    "description": "Engineering team",
    "owners": ["user.one@example.com"],
    "members": ["user.two@example.com"]
  },
  "ops": {
    "description": "Operations team",
    "visibility": "public",
    "owners": ["user.three@example.com"],
    "members": []
  }
}

TOML example:

[engineering]
description = "Engineering team"
owners = ["user.one@example.com"]
members = ["user.two@example.com"]

[ops]
description = "Operations team"
visibility = "public"
owners = ["user.three@example.com"]
members = []

docs.text:

docs.title: Message templates
docs.text:
Teams CLI supports templated messages using structured data in JSON, YAML, or TOML. A parser is automatically selected based on the data file extension.

The parser converts newlines to <br> in plain text, but preserves HTML as-is when HTML tags are detected.

docs.title: Mention syntax
docs.text:
Use @@identifier@@ to create mentions:

  • Email: @@user@domain.com@@
  • Special mentions for bulk sends: @@channel@@, @@team@@, @@this@@, @@everyone@@

Special mentions are resolved to the receiver automatically in bulk sends.

docs.title: Plain text example
docs.text:
Template (template.txt):

Hello {{.name}}!

Your order #{{.order}} is ready.
Thank you!

Data (data.json):

{
  "alex": {
    "name": "Alex",
    "order": "12345"
  },
  "blair": {
    "name": "Blair",
    "order": "67890"
  }
}

Data (data.yaml):

alex:
  name: Alex
  order: "12345"
blair:
  name: Blair
  order: "67890"

Data (data.toml):

[alex]
name = "Alex"
order = "12345"

[blair]
name = "Blair"
order = "67890"

docs.title: HTML content example
docs.text:
Template (template-html.txt):

<p>Hello <b>{{.name}}</b>!</p>

<p>Your order #{{.order}} is ready.</p>
<p>Click <a href="https://example.com/orders/{{.order}}">here</a> for details.</p>

docs.title: HTML tag detection
docs.text:
The parser treats content as HTML if it finds any of:

  • <p> and </p>
  • <b> and </b>
  • <i> and </i>
  • <br>
  • <a href="..."> and </a>

When HTML tags are detected, newlines are preserved.

docs.title: Channel message sample
docs.text:
Template (channel_message.txt):

Hello {{.name}}!
This is a channel mention @@channel@@
This is a personal mention {{.mention}}
This is a team mention @@team@@

Your order #{{.order}} is ready.
Thank you!

Data (channel_message_data.yaml):

general:
  name: Alex
  order: "12345"
  mention: "@@user.one@example.com@@"
announcements:
  name: Blair
  order: "67890"
  mention: "@@user.two@example.com@@"

docs.title: Chat message sample
docs.text:
Template (chat_message.txt):

Hello {{.name}}!
This is a this mention @@this@@

Your order #{{.order}} is ready.
Thank you!

Data (chat_message_data.yaml):

user.one@example.com:
  name: Alex
  order: "12345"
user.two@example.com:
  name: Blair
  order: "67890"

docs.title: Group chat sample
docs.text:
Template (group_chat_message.txt):

Hello {{.name}}!
This is a group chat mention @@everyone@@
This is a personal mention {{.mention}}
This is a duplicate group chat mention @@everyone@@

Your order #{{.order}} is ready.
Thank you!

Data (group_chat_message_data.yaml):

project chat:
  name: Alex
  order: "12345"
  mention: "@@user.one@example.com@@"
marketing chat:
  name: Blair
  order: "67890"
  mention: "@@user.two@example.com@@"
